objective: Produce one minimal, review-gated end-to-end experiment that proves the formal chain (compile -> three independent reviews -> decision -> finalization -> authorization -> run -> receipt -> analysis) actually closes on this platform, and that simultaneously serves as the F2 single-factor evidence: with PHY rate, routing policy, trace, topology and seed shared, execution.node_process_delay_s (0.0 vs 0.05) must move only the satellite node-processing stage.
context: This is an AUDIT work package, not a research contribution. It adds no algorithm, changes no simulator behaviour, and makes no performance claim.

It exists because the platform audit found the F2 mechanism implemented but not reachable from the official entry point. Commit 03aecfb added 'run --timeline-log' and the entry-point refusal; commit 8e69d79 made the independent recomputation separate node_process_s from decision_compute_s. This experiment is the end-to-end evidence that the repaired chain closes.

Design: strict 2-cell paired single factor execution.node_process_delay_s = 0.0 (control) vs 0.05 (f2). common_config pins links.isl_rate_mbps=10.0, routing.policy=hop, demand csv trace CODE/data/traffic/t1_step5_micro_ab.csv, scenario seed 7 / 8 satellites / 1 plane, execution.available_capacity_interval_s=0.1. The compiler enforces that the pair shares trace identity and controlled_signature.

execution.available_capacity_interval_s is deliberately non-null: metrics.py:334-340 falls back to the service-window denominator when no availability ledger exists, which makes utilization identically 1.0 and makes v2_analysis.py:337 flag every served ISL link as saturated. A run whose utilisation is reported must be sampled.

DECLARED BLOCKING LIMITATION the reviewers MUST assess and must not paper over: the 'f2' arm cannot be executed by the canonical remote runner today. F2 hard-requires a timeline sink (kernel.py:1145-1152); remote_job.py:304-309 builds the child command from exactly --config --out --authorization --launch-nonce --expect-run-id and never passes a timeline stream; run-remote.sh:44 rejects '--' as 'arbitrary commands are forbidden by the formal runner'. There is therefore no passthrough. The consequence is stated in the request claim_boundary and in R01/PROCEDURE.md section 4a rather than hidden.

Because of that limitation this batch executes both arms through the LOCAL CLI with the formal binding flags attached (PROCEDURE.md 4b). That path does exercise verify_authorization_for_leo_sim_v2_config and does write formal_run.json on natural_end, but it is NOT the canonical remote route and carries no VM provenance, and no artifact here may be cited as VM evidence.
The single-factor claim is bounded to this fixture. It is a structural/descriptive check, not an effect size, and it says nothing about any other scenario, load or topology.

REVIEWER PROVENANCE: the three review roles were executed by three separate cold-start agent sessions distinct from the producing session, at the reviewer ids recorded in each receipt. This satisfies the platform's existing practice (R06 used distinct GLM and Muse sessions); it is NOT human review and must not be described as independent institutional review.

learning or checkpoint artefacts (no learning arm exists in this batch)
results from any other experiment batch

authorization.json with status=AUTHORIZED covering exactly the two compiled cells

the f2 arm timeline stream with node_process_start/node_process_end milestones, plus its sha256-bound sidecar manifest
independent per-packet delay decomposition for both arms showing node_process_s and decision_compute_s as separate named terms
a written statement of which parts of the chain were and were not exercised (remote VM leg NOT exercised)

an effect-size, performance curve, threshold or causal claim about node processing delay
real subscriber traffic or a calibrated demand model
VM provenance for any artifact in this batch, or that the canonical remote runner executed the f2 arm
that the review gate was satisfied by human or institutional review
